claim: The /INT pulse length is not settled: the book gives 32 T (48K, +3 timing) and 36 T (128K, Pentagon) in CPU clocks at every speed; a board test here saw re-entry 38 T after the acknowledge. Keep handlers longer than 42 T before EI.
limit: The 38 T may be the 36 T pulse plus the acknowledge offset rather than a longer pulse; not separated by a test. docs/TECHNIQUES.md also says about 30 T.

evidence.source: I. Novak, Unraveling the ZX Spectrum Next, Vol 1 (2026; core 3.03.03), chapter 4
evidence.text: /INT in pulse mode goes low for a fixed count of CPU clocks, so at 28 MHz the pulse is eight times shorter in real time than at 3.5 MHz; one pulse serves every enabled source.
